verdicts.note: Genuinely mixed, so 0 is right. He is the challenger to an appointed incumbent and has never held county office. He also has the longer elected record: 12 years on the North Beach school board, nine as president [S1], plus chairing the drainage district [S7]. The 'Local. Proven. Trusted.' slogan in the scoring notes has no cited line in the dossier body; the score does not depend on it.

The only pole-b evidence is one plank: to 'continue supporting' the existing Coastal Community Action Program and the county housing authority [S2]. That is modest. It names no social housing, no tenant protections and no new public investment. Evidence points the other way too. He calls infrastructure investment important for housing [S2], a supply-side framing. He is endorsed by the Olympia Master Builders' Affordable Housing Council, which looks for candidates who favor 'a regulatory environment that allows our communities to grow and prosper' [S5]. The direction is still +1 on his own words, but the counter-signals and thin plank do not support medium.
Genuinely mixed, so 0 is right: 'committed to a strong budget', working toward 'a balanced budget', and 'the county needs to continue to invest in infrastructure' [S2].

Genuinely mixed, so 0 is right: community policing and the Resident Officer Program (police presence) alongside investment in crime-prevention programs [S2]. The basis also counts mental-health services, which the dossier files under health care rather than public safety [S2]; the score holds without it.

An appointed incumbent since May 16, 2026 [S6], with prior Cosmopolis School Board service [S1], so -1 fits. The basis says he is 'asking voters to let him continue', but the dossier body has no such quote (it appears only in the scoring notes) and cannot be verified from the cited sources. Drop that phrase from the basis. The score holds on incumbency alone, and five months in an appointed seat keeps it from reaching -2.

'Leadership that supports law enforcement, first responders' and homelessness addressed 'with compassion while maintaining accountability and protecting our neighborhoods' [S1]. The compassion qualifier keeps this at -1. It comes from one statement, so medium is right.

Generic 'responsible budgeting' [S1] and fire-department budget oversight to ensure 'taxpayer dollars were used efficiently and effectively' [S2]. Low confidence is right, given the generic language and his separate pledge to improve county services [S1].
